A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CursorCore work and provide readable main text, figures, tables and appendices. The added Appendix C and subsequent renumbering can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original CursorCore evaluations on APEval and other programming benchmarks, together with data-selection, code-format, target-area, reasoning and history-window experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations and ablations, including Tables 4–6 and the experimental figures in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Assistant-Conversation, the Programming-Instruct pipeline, CursorCore training and inference procedures, and appendix method variants are retained. Section 5.1 explicitly reiterates using base models and adds a rationale, without introducing a different procedure.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage remain unchanged: APEval, HumanEval/MBPP with additional tests, CanItEdit and Python HumanEvalFix. New Appendix C documents the existing APEval collection; its examples do not establish additional evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same comparator membership, including GPT-4o/GPT-4o-Mini on APEval and the corresponding DeepSeek-Coder, Yi-Coder and Qwen2.5-Coder baselines on other benchmarks. Newly cited GRACE and Overwatch are not added to the evaluations.

E3.justification: Both versions report 164 APEval samples, 41 per information combination, with the same Pass@1 tests, greedy decoding, evaluation prompts and training settings. Appendix C newly describes annotation, selection and balancing of this benchmark; it does not report a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The data-source, code-format, target-area, thought-process and history-window analyses are retained with unchanged evidence. New Figure 13 illustrates benchmark inputs and intended edits, without adding a model-output case study or experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The parenthesized evaluation scores continue to distinguish extra-test results from base-test results, rather than report uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 4–6 and the retained experimental plots contain unchanged results. For example, Table 4 reports CursorCore-QW2.5-1.5B averages of 50.0 on base tests and 46.3 on extra tests in both versions. The new benchmark illustrations do not report additional model outcomes.

T1.justification: The framework element definitions and code-modification representations are retained. No mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: Assistant-Conversation, Programming-Instruct and its 219K samples, APEval, and CursorCore's performance relative to similarly sized models. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds substantive reasoning about selecting history-dependent examples and the difficulty of obtaining realistic traces for every task and information combination. Section 5.1 adds a rationale for fine-tuning base models. Existing result interpretations and the limitations appendix are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix C documents providing annotators with function specifications, recording their work, manually extracting traces, and adding or discarding traces to balance information combinations. These details improve documentation of the existing benchmark; implementation settings, prompts and resource-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly acknowledges prior incorporation of editing histories and instructions, adding GRACE (Gupta et al., 2023) and Overwatch (Zhang et al., 2022). The Liger Kernel reference receives a bibliographic update, without a substantive change in positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix C and limited explanatory prose about framework integration, model selection and training-data lengths. Cross-references and subsequent appendix labels are updated. The main section order and most wording remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 13 with two APEval examples and expands the captions of Figure 2 and Table 1. Existing figures and tables are retained, with subsequent figure renumbering and local page reflow; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v1 briefly describes APEval construction in Section 3.1; v2 explains recording, trace extraction, selection and balancing, and illustrates the intended tasks in Figure 13. These additions, clearer captions and acknowledgment of related historical-edit work modestly improve transparency and readability. The experimental evidence and acknowledged evaluation limitations remain unchanged.
